newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rainstorms sweep French Riviera, Corsica.
newsitem.headline: Rainstorms sweep French Riviera, Corsica.

text.p: Rainstorms swept the French Riviera and Corsica on Sunday, flooding roads and cutting short the 24-hour Bol d'Or international motorcycle race after it was marred by falls.

The race at Le Castellet north of Marseille was twice suspended by heavy rain, once after French rider Serge Vieira was seriously injured in a fall. Organisers eventually halted it an hour before the end.
Water ran one-metre (three-foot) high through the town of Cogolin and the village of Gassin, a jet-set haunt near the resort of Saint-Tropez. Some cars were swept away.
Helicopters hoisted to safety a few people stranded on the roof of mobile homes.
On the holiday island of Corsica bridges were swept off in Galewrias and Calenzana. Some roads were cut off arounf Ajaccio and 17 people were evacuated from their homes in the Balagne region.
